project-charter.title: Project Charter & Real-World Observation

cards.title: Client Brief & Objective
cards.body: Atlas Cycles Engineering Department has assigned you to analyze and design the cotter joint connecting the pedal crank arm to the bottom-bracket spindle/axle in a standard utility bicycle.

cards.title: Real-World Mechanical Observation
cards.body: In a bicycle crank assembly, human downward force on the pedal creates a driving torque on the crank arm. This torque must be transmitted into the spindle without relative rotation or joint loosening during pedaling cycles.

cards.title: Deliverables & Scope
items: Identify the power transmission path from pedal to axle.
Label cotter joint components on Engineering Asset EA-10.
Analyze wedge action, torque capacity, shear stress, and crushing stress.
Determine the Factor of Safety (FoS) and render an engineering decision.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have read and understood the EC-10 Project Charter for Bicycle Cotter Joint Design.

power-transmission-path.title: Power Transmission Path Identification
power-transmission-path.prompt: Analyze the mechanical sequence through which human muscular force applied at the bicycle pedal is converted into rotational torque delivered to the drive chainring.

mcq.question: Which sequence correctly describes the flow of power and torque in a bicycle crank mechanism?

options.label: Pedal Force → Crank Arm → Cotter Joint → Spindle/Axle → Chainring
Pedal Force → Spindle/Axle → Cotter Joint → Crank Arm → Chainring
Chainring → Cotter Joint → Crank Arm → Pedal Force → Spindle
Pedal Force → Chainring → Cotter Joint → Spindle → Crank Arm

component-identification.title: Cotter Joint Component Identification
component-identification.description: Student engineering asset showing the bicycle pedal-crank-spindle assembly and cotter joint construction.

labels.feedback: Pedal crank arm transmitting foot force into torque.
Hub of crank arm with transverse hole for cotter pin.
Bottom bracket axle shaft with flat cotter seat.
Wedge-shaped tapered steel pin driven into joint.
Nut securing the threaded end of the cotter pin.
Drive sprocket delivering power to bicycle rear chain.
Threaded pedal spindle mounted at crank outer end.

working-principle.title: Working Principle & Joint Function
working-principle.prompt: A cotter joint uses a wedge-shaped, tapered pin driven through a transverse hole formed partly in the crank eye and partly in a flat seat cut into the spindle.

mcq.question: What is the primary mechanical function of the tapered cotter pin in a bicycle crank joint?

options.label: To lock the crank and spindle together by wedge action, preventing relative rotation and transmitting torque.
To act as a flexible spring that absorbs shock loads during braking.
To permanently weld the crank to the spindle without disassembling capability.
To allow the crank arm to rotate freely around the spindle during pedaling.

torque-calculation.title: Applied Pedal Force & Torque Analysis
given: Design Rider Downward Pedal Force (F) = 600 N

questions.label: 1. Material Selection & Yield Strengths
questions.placeholder: State the selected material (e.g. Plain Carbon Steel C30/C45) and yield tensile strength (Syt) assumed for the cotter pin and crank.

questions.label: 2. Allowable Shear and Bearing Stresses
questions.placeholder: State allowable shear stress (tau_all = 0.5 * Syt / FoS) and allowable crushing/bearing stress (sigma_b_all = 1.2 * Syt / FoS).

questions.label: 3. Factor of Safety & Taper Assumptions
questions.placeholder: Specify chosen Factor of Safety (Ns = 2.0 to 2.5) and standard cotter taper ratio (e.g., 1 in 24 or 1 in 30).

cotter-design-calculation.title: Cotter Joint Design & Stress Calculations
given: Spindle Diameter at Cotter Seat (d) = 16 mm

strength-safety-check.title: Strength & Factor of Safety Check
given: Cotter Material Allowable Shear Strength (tau_all) = 75.0 N/mm²
Cotter Material Allowable Crushing Strength (sigma_b_all) = 150.0 N/mm²

options.title: ACCEPT DESIGN AS SAFE
options.description: Calculated shear stress (68.36 N/mm²) and crushing stress (136.72 N/mm²) remain strictly below allowable material limits, yielding a Factor of Safety > 1.0 under maximum pedaling torque.

options.title: REJECT DESIGN / INCREASE COTTER THICKNESS
options.description: If peak standing-pedal shock loads exceed 900 N, shearing or localized bearing deformation occurs. Recommend increasing cotter thickness to 10 mm and using hardened steel.

questions.label: 1. Executive Summary & Design Decision
questions.placeholder: State whether the cotter joint design is safe or unsafe, reporting the calculated FoS against allowable limits.

questions.label: 2. Critical Failure Mode Analysis
questions.placeholder: Explain which failure mode (cotter shear, cotter crushing, or spindle notch shearing) is critical for this bicycle joint.

questions.label: 3. Manufacturing & Maintenance Recommendations
questions.placeholder: Provide practical recommendations regarding cotter taper fitting, nut tightening torque, and wear prevention during service.
